name: Te Wahipounamu – South West New Zealand
description: Te Wāhipounamu, "the place of greenstone," fills the south-west corner of New Zealand's South Island with about 26,000 square kilometres of wilderness. It links four national parks, including Fiordland and Aoraki / Mount Cook. Glaciers carved its fjords, cliffs, lakes and waterfalls, and forests of ancient trees, some over 800 years old, shelter cheeky kea parrots and the rare, flightless takahe.
